messages.author: e66baf722e0aed3f
messages.subject: Error in .Call(Module__classes_info, xp) :  Cannot allocate vector of length ...
parts:
Hello all,

I have debugged my code to the point that it seems ready to compile and then run repeatedly into the following error:

COMPILING MODEL 'mlirt' NOW.
Error in .Call(Module__classes_info, xp) :
  cannot allocate vector of length 1790997466

I have used the command memory.limit() to set the memory as high as it can go, but I'm not sure what else to do. I've attached my code and my data. I've seen several threads that report running into memory challenges with fixed effects, and I'm estimating a heirarchical IRT model with both fixed and random effects.

Any suggestions would be greatly appreciated. Thank you so much.
Shauna

messages.subject: Past the Allocation Error... Onto Dimensional (Definitional) Difficulties...
parts:
I have gone through the code and successfully moved past that error, but now I have run into the following:

STARTING SAMPLER FOR MODEL 'mlirt' NOW.
Error : mismatch in number dimensions declared and found in context; processing stage=data initialization; variable name=N; dims declared=(); dims found=(81384)

My data and transformed data pieces of the model are as follows:

data {
   int<lower=1> N;              // number of responses
   int<lower=1> J;              // number of students
   int<lower=1> K;              // number of items
   int<lower=1> P;              // number of parent items
   int<lower=1> L;              // num key content elements
   int<lower=1> M;              // num item models
   int<lower=1> T;    // num forms (operation and qsc combination)
  
   int<lower=0,upper=1> C[M];      // binary form characteristics
   int<lower=0,upper=1> L1[M];      // binary form characteristics
   int<lower=0,upper=1> L2[M];      // binary form characteristics
   int<lower=0,upper=1> L3[M];      // binary form characteristics
   int<lower=0,upper=1> L4[M];      // binary form characteristics
   int<lower=1,upper=M> cc[M];  // characteristics for item model m
   int<lower=1,upper=M> tt[M];  // template for item model m
   int<lower=1,upper=P> mm[P];  // item model for parent p 
   int<lower=1,upper=K> pp[K];  // family for item k
   int<lower=1,upper=J> jj[N];  // student giving response n
   int<lower=1,upper=K> kk[N];  // item for response n
   int<lower=0,upper=1> y[N];   // correctness for response n
}
transformed data {
   int obs;
   int peeps;
   int items;
   int parents;
   int imodels;
   int templates;
   int fixed;
   vector[M] z;           // predictors for item models (form level)
   matrix[P,L] x;        // predictors for families (key content)
   obs<-81834;
   peeps<-1522;
   items<-902;
   parents<-45;
   imodels<-27;
   templates<-15;
   fixed<-4;
   for (m in 1:imodels){
    for (p in 1:parents){
     for (n in 1:obs){
        z[m]<-C[cc[pp[kk[n]]]];
 
        x[p,1]<-L1[pp[kk[n]]];
        x[p,2]<-L2[pp[kk[n]]];
        x[p,3]<-L3[pp[kk[n]]];
        x[p,4]<-L4[pp[kk[n]]];
   }}}
}



I do have a variable in my dataset named "N" that is an index for the number of people. In fact, all of the variables that are in that first data block are the names of variables in my dataset, and all of them are indices for observations, students, items, etc. which correspond to levels and components of my calibration model. Is it the naming of my variables that is causing the problem?

Thank you for all your help... I'm sorry I feel like I'm stumbling through.
S

On Thursday, March 31, 2016 at 12:30:11 PM UTC-4, Shauna Sweet wrote:
I have gone through the code and successfully moved past that error, but now I have run into the following:

STARTING SAMPLER FOR MODEL 'mlirt' NOW.
Error : mismatch in number dimensions declared and found in context; processing stage=data initialization; variable name=N; dims declared=(); dims found=(81384)

My data and transformed data pieces of the model are as follows:

data {
   int<lower=1> N;              // number of responses
...

I do have a variable in my dataset named "N" that is an index for the number of people. In fact, all of the variables that are in that first data block are the names of variables in my dataset, and all of them are indices for observations, students, items, etc. which correspond to levels and components of my calibration model. Is it the naming of my variables that is causing the problem?

No. Inside R, you overwrote the symbol N with a vector that is of length 81384 and then passed that N to Stan. That is what the error message above is telling you.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Past the Allocation Error... Onto Dimensional (Definitional) Difficulties...
parts:
There's no data file in R. You pass data to stan using data=....
And whatever the value of N is when that's called is what Stan
gets. In your case, you're setting N to an 81,384-element list before
calling Stan.

If you feel like you're stumbling through, I would very strongly
urge you to start with a simpler model to see how things work without
so many moving pieces.

- Bob
